kurz: Mushrooms are around 90 % water and bring plenty of umami: only once the water has gone do they turn brown and savoury.
bild_im_kopf: Like a sponge full of broth: squeeze it out first, then roast.
was_passiert: When heated, mushrooms first release a lot of water and shrink. As long as they sit in their own juice, they cook at 100 °C. Once the water has evaporated, they brown in fat and develop roasted flavours. Their cell walls stay firm, so they rarely turn mushy.
warum_wichtig: [[pilze-braten|Frying mushrooms]] patiently until the water is gone gives flavour instead of grey rubbery pieces.
faustregeln: Fry mushrooms in a large pan with room to spare.
Salt only once they have browned.
